case.scope: Project example case; facts are reported by the case, not independently confirmed clinical observations.

Compound::DB05025.name: Arimoclomol
Compound::DB05025.warning: Decreased weight and diarrhea occurred in the labeled NPC setting with miglustat. Further loss matters after Alex fell from 86 to 77.5 kg; incidence in ALS or local delivery is unknown.
Compound::DB05025.medication_check: The label reports no CYP1A2 inhibition or induction in vitro and flags OCT2 substrates. ORARIALS-01 stratified on stable riluzole use. Neither source establishes the safety of the proposed route.
Compound::DB05025.contrary: ORARIALS-01 found no improvement in combined function and survival; gastrointestinal events and discontinuations were more frequent with arimoclomol.
Compound::DB05025.change: A controlled functional benefit with a credible exposure rationale and tolerability despite weight loss would materially change this assessment.

Compound::DB06151.name: Acetylcysteine
Compound::DB06151.warning: The inhalation label warns about bronchospasm and an increased volume of liquefied secretions that may require suction if cough is inadequate. Reduced supine FVC makes airway clearance consequential; coughing on liquids does not prove an ineffective cough.
Compound::DB06151.medication_check: The inhalation label and ALS trial do not establish a riluzole interaction or compatibility with local administration. Respiratory obstruction from aerosol exposure is distinct from drug-induced respiratory depression.
Compound::DB06151.contrary: A 110-person ALS trial of subcutaneous acetylcysteine found no significant overall survival or progression benefit. The limb-onset subgroup estimate included no effect.
Compound::DB06151.change: A prespecified limb-onset study with measurable target engagement, respiratory tolerability and functional benefit would strengthen the case.

Compound::DB14533.name: Zinc chloride
Compound::DB14533.warning: The parenteral nutrition additive carries a copper-deficiency warning including myeloneuropathy, relevant to existing weakness. Direct undiluted IV or IM injection is contraindicated for this acidic product; the case specifies neither that product nor those routes.
Compound::DB14533.medication_check: No direct riluzole combination evidence was established. Baseline copper, zinc and renal status are unknown. The labeled product is an IV admixture component.
Compound::DB14533.contrary: Zinc-depleted SOD was toxic in cultured motor neurons. That finding does not show that zinc chloride restores functional SOD1 in people with ALS.
Compound::DB14533.change: Demonstrated metal deficiency, intracellular target engagement, route-specific toxicology and benefit distinct from nutritional repletion would be needed.

Compound::DB00148.name: Creatine
Compound::DB00148.medication_check: The ALS trial reported no important adverse reactions in that study, but it does not establish a riluzole interaction profile or local-route safety. Elevated creatine kinase is not evidence of creatine deficiency.
Compound::DB00148.contrary: A randomized trial of 175 ALS patients found no improvement in survival or decline in function, including muscle and respiratory measures.
Compound::DB00148.change: Evidence of an exposure-dependent benefit in a prospectively defined phenotype, plus renal and formulation safety data, would change the ranking.

Compound::DB14487.name: Zinc acetate
Compound::DB14487.warning: Prolonged zinc acetate use has caused copper deficiency with myeloneuropathy. New neurological weakness would be hard to distinguish from ALS progression. The oral capsule also needs a swallowing-feasibility assessment.
Compound::DB14487.medication_check: The Wilson disease label addresses copper depletion, not coadministration with riluzole for ALS. Copper and renal status and suitability for local delivery are unknown.
Compound::DB14487.contrary: The SOD metallation experiment was in motor neuron culture, not a clinical zinc acetate trial. The label concerns Wilson disease.
Compound::DB14487.change: A patient-relevant metallation deficit, comparative evidence against other zinc forms and a safety study measuring copper and neurological outcomes would change the case.

Compound::DB01593.name: Zinc (elemental record)
Compound::DB01593.warning: Excess oral zinc can deplete copper; resulting neurological deficits matter with existing hand weakness. This record does not specify a formulation.
Compound::DB01593.medication_check: The NIH zinc review is not a riluzole combination study. Neither the product nor actual metal exposure is known.
Compound::DB01593.contrary: Cellular evidence on SOD metallation does not establish human benefit for elemental zinc.
Compound::DB01593.change: Identify the actual formulation, metal status, combination data and clinical response.

Compound::DB12310.name: Trehalose
Compound::DB12310.warning: In HEALEY ALS, serious adverse events occurred in 16% on trehalose versus 7% on regimen-only placebo. Respiratory failure was the most common cause of death; investigators attributed no deaths to the drug. This is a signal to review in a patient with limited respiratory reserve, not proof of drug-induced respiratory depression.
Compound::DB12310.medication_check: Stratification by riluzole use is not a formal drug-interaction study. Safety of the hypothetical local route remains unknown.
Compound::DB12310.contrary: HEALEY found no evidence of slower ALS progression or significant secondary biomarker benefits at the tested exposure.
Compound::DB12310.change: A materially different exposure rationale with demonstrated benefit and reassuring respiratory outcome data would be needed.

Compound::DB01065.name: Melatonin
Compound::DB01065.warning: The Circadin prolonged-release formulation must be swallowed whole. Feasibility is uncertain in Alex, who coughs on thin liquids. This is a formulation warning, not a blanket veto on melatonin.
Compound::DB01065.medication_check: The European product information does not establish safety of combined local delivery with riluzole.
Compound::DB01065.contrary: A human ALS study of rectal melatonin reported tolerability and a biomarker change. Clinical functional benefit was not established. The whole-tablet issue concerns the separate prolonged-release oral formulation.
Compound::DB01065.change: Verify the intended formulation and riluzole interaction and find controlled ALS outcome evidence.

Compound::DB01017.name: Minocycline
Compound::DB01017.warning: Documented harm in ALS: the treated group lost 1.30 ALSFRS-R points/month versus 1.04 on placebo (p=0.005). Preserving function is directly relevant to Alex's limb-onset disease.
Compound::DB01017.medication_check: A small trial coadministered minocycline with riluzole at Alex's 50 mg twice-daily dose. It did not establish a serious drug-pair interaction or the safety of another route.
Compound::DB01017.contrary: The larger phase III trial found faster functional decline. The limited pairwise tolerability data do not resolve that harm.
Compound::DB01017.change: A materially different intervention would need strong human evidence that addresses the randomized harm finding.

Compound::DB01043.name: Memantine
Compound::DB01043.warning: Kidney function and tolerability under the assumed route remain unknown.
Compound::DB01043.medication_check: The label describes minimal CYP1A2 inhibition in vitro. A pilot coadministered memantine and riluzole. Neither establishes safety for Alex under the proposed delivery assumption.
Compound::DB01043.contrary: The randomized phase 2B study found no difference in ALS progression or neuropsychiatric outcomes.
Compound::DB01043.change: A reproducible functional benefit, documented renal status and exposure-specific tolerability would change this assessment.
